extracted.intended_audience: K-12 and higher-education school administrators, educators, and NEA affiliates (Title IX coordinators, HR/legal staff, and teachers)
extracted.subtask_description: Summarizes school obligations under the Department of Education's new Title IX final rule (effective Aug 1, 2024), including protections for LGBTQ+ people, pregnancy/lactation rights, and required grievance/response procedures. Intended to guide policy drafting and implementation at K-12 and postsecondary institutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on discrimination based on sexual orientation and gender identity
rubrics_metrics.description: Discrimination on the basis of sexual orientation and gender identity (as well as discrimination based on sex stereotypes and sex characteristics) is prohibited sex discrimination under Title IX.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This follows ED's long-standing interpretation and the Supreme Court's rationale in Bostock; while not a new interpretation, the final rule is the first time these explicit protections are formalized in Title IX regulations, giving them the force of law. See 34 C.F.R. §§ 106.2, 106.10.

rubrics_metrics.name: More-than-de-minimis-harm standard for sex-based differential treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: Schools may not separate or treat any person differently based on sex in a manner that subjects them to 'more than de minimis harm,' except in limited circumstances authorized under Title IX.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preventing someone from participating in a program or activity consistent with their gender identity is characterized as causing more than de minimis harm and is therefore prohibited. See 34 C.F.R. § 106.31(a)(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on sex-segregated activities and facilities (prohibition on blanket bans)
rubrics_metrics.description: Transgender bathroom bans and other blanket denials of participation or use of facilities based on gender identity are prohibited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under the rule, bans on use of school facilities or participation in activities consistent with a student’s or educator’s gender identity cause more than de minimis harm and are disallowed. See 34 C.F.R. § 106.31(a)(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Repeated misgendering/deadnaming may constitute sex-based harassment
rubrics_metrics.description: Repeated misgendering or deadnaming that is 'severe or pervasive' can be prohibited sex-based harassment; isolated or 'stray' remarks generally are not harassment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whether verbal conduct like misgendering is harassment is fact-specific. A 'stray remark' or single misuse of language is not considered harassment, but repeated misgendering that is severe or pervasive may be. See 34 C.F.R. § 106.2; 89 Fed. Reg. 33516 (Apr. 29, 2024).

rubrics_metrics.name: State law preemption by Title IX
rubrics_metrics.description: Title IX requirements, including protections based on sexual orientation and gender identity, preempt conflicting state laws; schools must comply with Title IX even if state law conflicts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although federal law generally supersedes conflicting state law, some states have announced noncompliance and litigation has been filed; unless and until enjoined, schools and districts must follow Title IX. See 34 C.F.R. § 106.6.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protections for pregnancy and related conditions (including lactation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Schools may not discriminate based on pregnancy or related conditions; the rule clarifies protections to include lactation and requires lactation time and space for students and employees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rule builds on longstanding requirements since 1975 and updates them to explicitly include lactation as a related condition and require access to clean, private lactation spaces and reasonable lactation breaks. See 34 C.F.R. § 106.40 and § 106.57.

rubrics_metrics.name: Educator obligation to notify students of pregnancy-related rights
rubrics_metrics.description: When a student or their parent informs a school employee of the student's pregnancy or related condition, the employee must provide the Title IX coordinator's contact information and advise the student that the coordinator can help ensure equal access.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Information about the student's pregnancy must be kept confidential. See 34 C.F.R. § 106.40(b)(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Student rights for pregnancy and related conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Students must be informed of the school's obligations and nondiscrimination notice, offered individualized reasonable modifications, allowed voluntary leave for medically necessary periods, and ensured access to a clean, private lactation space.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific required actions include: informing the student about nondiscrimination and disclosure restrictions; offering reasonable individualized modifications; allowing voluntary leave at least for medically necessary periods; and ensuring lactation space. See 34 C.F.R. § 106.40(b)(3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Employee rights for pregnancy, lactation, and leave
rubrics_metrics.description: Employees must be provided reasonable break time for lactation and access to a clean, private lactation space; employees lacking other leave options must be given voluntary unpaid leave for a reasonable period and reinstated to same or comparable position.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employees also retain rights under the Pregnant Workers Fairness Act (PWFA) and the PUMP Act. See 34 C.F.R. § 106.57(e)(1)-(2) and § 106.57(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Grievance process must cover all sex-based discrimination (not just sexual harassment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Schools must apply their Title IX grievance process to all complaints of sex discrimination, including discrimination based on sex stereotypes, sex characteristics, pregnancy or related conditions, sexual orientation, and gender identity, and must address retaliation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This expands the scope beyond prior rules that focused primarily on sexual harassment. See 34 C.F.R. § 106.10 and § 106.71.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written grievance procedures incorporating due process
rubrics_metrics.description: All schools must adopt written grievance procedures that incorporate the due process requirements set out in the new rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grievance procedures must be in writing and comply with the procedural requirements in 34 C.F.R. § 106.45(a)(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Broader definition of hostile environment harassment
rubrics_metrics.description: Harassment creating a hostile environment is 'unwelcome sex-based conduct that, based on the totality of the circumstances, is subjectively and objectively offensive and is so severe or pervasive that it limits or denies a person's ability to participate in or benefit from the [school's] education program or activity.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The new definition expands scope from the 2020 rule; conduct need not be sexual to violate Title IX. Repeated sex-based offensive jokes may qualify if widespread or repetitive enough to be pervasive. See 34 C.F.R. § 106.2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to respond 'promptly and effectively' to conduct that may reasonably constitute sex discrimination
rubrics_metrics.description: Schools must respond promptly and effectively to any conduct they know of that may reasonably constitute sex discrimination, not merely to conduct about which they have 'actual knowledge' under a deliberately indifferent standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This raises schools' affirmative obligations, including taking steps to notify students of rights and address barriers to reporting. See 34 C.F.R. § 106.44(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Employee reporting requirements and handling of oral reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Complaints of possible sex discrimination may be reported orally; schools must respond to oral reports. Specific reporting obligations vary by level: at K-12, any non-confidential employee who receives information about possible sex discrimination must notify the Title IX coordinator; at higher ed, non-confidential employees with authority to take corrective action and certain administrators must notify, while other non-confidential employees must either notify or provide information about how to contact the coordinator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Schools may designate 'confidential employees' whose communications are privileged or confidential under law. See 34 C.F.R. § 106.2 and § 106.44(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Privacy protections for personally identifiable information
rubrics_metrics.description: The rule prohibits schools from disclosing personally identifiable information obtained in complying with Title IX, with limited exceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limited exceptions include, for example, disclosures to the parent of a minor. See 34 C.F.R. § 106.44(j).

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to offer supportive measures to complainants and respondents
rubrics_metrics.description: Schools are required to offer supportive measures to complainants (whether or not a formal complaint is filed) and to respondents if needed during grievance procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supportive measures can include counseling, assignment extensions, restrictions on contact, leaves of absence, training, and other measures, provided they do not unreasonably burden either party. See 34 C.F.R. § 106.44(f)(1)(ii) and § 106.44(g).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of a single-investigator model permitted (so long as no conflicts/bias)
rubrics_metrics.description: The rule allows the Title IX coordinator or investigator to also serve as decisionmaker if they have no conflicts of interest or bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This departs from the 2020 rules which required separate investigators and decisionmakers. See 34 C.F.R. § 106.45(b)(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonably prompt timeframes required for investigation and decision-making stages
rubrics_metrics.description: The rule no longer prescribes specific time periods but requires schools to set 'reasonably prompt timeframes' for all major stages of investigation and decision-making.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Schools must adopt and follow these timelines in their written grievance procedures; the rule removes the previously required specified response periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voluntary informal resolution permitted with a key exception
rubrics_metrics.description: Schools may allow voluntary informal resolution of complaints at any stage except that informal resolution is never allowed for complaints that an employee engaged in sex-based harassment of a K-12 student.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Informal resolution remains optional and cannot be used in the specified K-12 employee-on-student harassment context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training requirements for employees, investigators, decisionmakers, and coordinators
rubrics_metrics.description: Schools must provide annual training to all employees about the school's Title IX obligations and the scope of conduct that constitutes sex discrimination; additional training is required for investigators, decisionmakers, and Title IX coordinators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training must cover applicable notification duties and the scope of prohibited conduct. See 34 C.F.R. § 106.8(d). ED has published resources and model language to aid schools in drafting nondiscrimination policies and grievance procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and role of 'confidential employees'
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Confidential employees' are those whose communications are privileged or confidential under federal or state law, and other employees a school may designate as confidential for purposes of providing services related to sex discrimination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designation affects reporting obligations: confidential employees are not required to notify the Title IX coordinator when they receive reports. See 34 C.F.R. § 106.2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affirmative obligations to notify students of rights and address reporting barriers
rubrics_metrics.description: Schools must take affirmative steps to notify students of their Title IX rights and to address barriers to reporting sex discrimination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requirement is part of the expanded 'prompt and effective' response obligation and reflects an expectation that schools proactively ensure access to reporting and supports. See 34 C.F.R. § 106.44(a).
